sources.title: The Nonequispaced FFT and its Applications: A Mini Course at Helsinki University of Technology
sources.locator: Part I, PDF slides 31–69: the complete relevant sequence from one- and d-dimensional Poisson summation through the NFFT definitions, Gaussian gridding, analytic alias/truncation error estimates, and complexity summary was read.

contents.name: Poisson summation for the one-dimensional periodisation
contents.support: The local proof verifies the Gaussian Schwartz hypotheses and fixes the same negative-sign 2π convention before using the full Poisson-summation supplier.

contents.name: Poisson summation for a d-dimensional periodisation
contents.support: The algorithm uses a separable product kernel and a tensor-product grid; each coordinate identity is proved from the local one-dimensional formula.

contents.name: Type-1 and type-2 nonuniform Fourier sums
contents.support: The finite sums and point/mode roles are specified locally with a normalized torus and explicit signs.

contents.name: Taylor-expansion NFFT and its derivative error estimate
contents.reason: This is a separate Taylor-window approximation with its own derivative bounds; the approved local algorithm uses Gaussian spreading and proves its own alias and truncation terms.

contents.name: Gaussian-window ansatz, deconvolution, and oversampled FFT
contents.support: The local procedure adopts this factorization structure, fixes the period and normalization, and adds certified finite truncation and arithmetic branches.

contents.name: Sparse matrix factorization and conjugate-transpose type 2
contents.support: The local proof writes the exact finite gridding matrix and its conjugate transpose, then separately bounds its entrywise error.

contents.name: Multivariate separable window
contents.support: The procedure uses a coordinatewise product Gaussian and proves the finite-grid cost and error with fixed dimension.

contents.name: Gaussian-window aliasing and truncation error estimate
contents.support: The source decomposition is used as a proof guide; this theorem derives its own explicit lattice alias sum and finite Gaussian tail bound.

contents.name: Compact B-spline window error theorem
contents.reason: The B-spline window is a distinct compact-support kernel and has a separate alias proof; no B-spline implementation or accuracy claim is part of the approved Gaussian branch.

contents.name: Parameterized Gaussian-window error estimate
contents.support: The lecture's specialized Gaussian estimate is not copied; the local theorem proves a wider parameterized bound from explicit alias and omitted-grid sums.

contents.name: NFFT operation-count and precision summary
contents.support: The local count separates the oversampled FFT and compact spreading work and states fixed-dimension, bounded-width hypotheses.

sources.title: Accelerating the Nonuniform Fast Fourier Transform
sources.locator: Complete paper read: SIAM Review 46(3), 2004, printed pp. 443–454 (PDF pp. 1–12), including definitions, Gaussian gridding, all examples, conclusions, and references.

contents.name: Type-1 and type-2 finite Fourier-sum definitions
contents.support: The local definition uses the same source/target roles and states its own 2π normalization, sign, domains, and type-3 extension.

contents.name: Periodic heat kernel, smoothing, and Fourier deconvolution
contents.support: The periodic Gaussian and positive Fourier multiplier agree with the local kernel after an explicit change of scale.

contents.name: Source-centered Gaussian fast gridding and tensor-product construction
contents.locator: §3, printed pp. 447–448; equations (16) and the type-1 gridding steps
contents.support: The local procedure adopts separable Gaussian spreading and oversampled FFT structure while proving each of its success bounds and failure branches.

contents.name: The paper's explicit statement that detailed error analysis is elsewhere
contents.support: The local theorem does not treat the paper's parameter summary as proof and supplies the full deterministic alias, truncation, and arithmetic argument.

contents.name: Empirical gridding-error plots and parameter table
contents.reason: These are numerical observations for selected samples and oversampling ratios, not a uniform proof; the local accuracy guarantee is derived from exact finite sums and explicit tails.

contents.name: Hardware timing and direct-method performance comparisons
contents.reason: Machine timing and break-even measurements depend on the tested hardware and implementation; the local page states only a proved arithmetic-operation count.

contents.name: MRI radial sampling and type-2/type-1 reconstruction
contents.support: The source motivates the MRI context; the example uses a small exact finite data set and computes its Fourier samples directly.

contents.name: Distinction between the discrete transform and acquisition or quadrature choices
contents.locator: Remark 1, printed p. 444, and Conclusions, printed p. 452
contents.support: The page defines only the finite transform and keeps quadrature, data acquisition, and application-specific reconstruction weights separate.

sources.title: NUFFT User's Guide, Version 1.2
sources.locator: Complete 13-page manual read; §1 and §§4–7 specify all three transform types, input domains, and the type-3 range-dependent workspace estimate.

contents.name: One-, two-, and three-dimensional type-1, type-2, and type-3 sums
contents.support: The local definition fixes its own normalized torus/sign convention and states the same three finite sum types.

contents.name: Type-3 source and arbitrary frequency-list inputs
contents.support: The local type-3 definition uses an explicit finite list of real frequencies and states that no frequency scaling is implicit.

contents.name: Type-3 workspace depends on source and frequency ranges
contents.support: The local definition makes no type-1 complexity transfer and requires a separate frequency-space scale/product analysis.
